liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step** (2 reviews): Forgetful singing in the opener suggests Jerry was in a happy mood that day; Reviewer loves the Half-Step opener [18][20]
- **Lost Sailor** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out the Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance pairing as well worth hearing; Bobby sang a line about freedom not coming easy and a 25 cent cup of coffee, lifting a grieving listener [19][22]
- **Drums** (2 other sources): Weir stays on stage with Billy and Mickey before Drums begins; Weir remains on stage with Billy and Mickey before Drums [6][7]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Jerry fumbles three verses, but his and Brent's instrumental section is amazing [19]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Maybe a small stumble in Crazy Fingers, since the band had just started playing it [23]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): The transition from Black Peter into Good Lovin' is called excellent [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bob & Brent Jam**: rare: 4 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-07-25.137192.nak300.schley.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 166 min [1]. Said about its sound: Minor tape damage in the left channel affects the first 2:37 of Candyman [1]
- **gd1982-07-25.senn421.vita.minches.80279.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording quality is described as outstanding, putting you in the room; Reviewer calls the sound good [21][23]
- **gd1982-07-25.156345.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 166 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd1982-07-25.167342.shure.sm57.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496_202404**: audience recording; 20 songs; 169 min [7]
- **gd1982-07-25.fob.senn421.wise.miller.102502.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 167 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [10]
- **gd82-07-25.fob.18481.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [12]. Said about its sound: Sound is fine to good and easy to listen to; Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound great [17][18]
- **gd1982-07-25.156497.s2.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: source not stated; 12 songs; 95 min [15]

## Around the show

- An airport sits behind the stage at Tempe's Compton Terrace [16]
- Heads who traveled from Tempe to Red Rocks two days later raved about this show [26]
- Reviewer rates this Crazy Fingers below the Ventura or Red Rocks versions, though Tempe was always fun [16]
- Reviewer recalls the 1980 Compton Terrace second set as the best of the Tempe shows [16]
- Reviewer says the Compendium undersold this show, calling it a fine representation of a 1982 show [17]
- Reviewer ranks it among the top shows of 1982 [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-07-25.137192.nak300.schley.flac1644**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > TDK-MA (Set 1), Maxell-MX (Set 2), FOB recording by Brian Schley. [1]. Also: Taped with a Nakamichi 300, Schley source; patched using ID-80279 and ID-18481 for the encore [1]
- **gd1982-07-25.senn421.vita.minches.80279.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by David Minches; source: 2 Sennheiser 421s> Sony D-5 (TDK MA-R) > MAC [3]
- **gd1982-07-25.156345.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MA-R 90) [6]
- **gd1982-07-25.167342.shure.sm57.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496_202404**: taped by Ken Kelley; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ken Kelley's Master Audience Cassettes; Shure SM-57 mics > JVC KD-2 w/Super ANRS (Maxell XLII-S90) [7]. Also: Shure SM57 source from Ken Kelley's master cassettes, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Sennheiser 421 patches in Estimated Prophet, Drums and Space [7]
- **gd1982-07-25.fob.senn421.wise.miller.102502.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B) [10]. Also: Mr. Wise used Sennheiser 421 microphones, which reviewer prefers over Nakamichi shotguns [24]
- **gd82-07-25.fob.18481.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise?; source: Audience Recording [12]
- **gd1982-07-25.156497.s2.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: taped by Concert recording by Rip Tompkins, & with thanks to Richie Stankiewicz!; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 04/2022; source: BeyerDynamic mics > Sony TC-D5M > TDK MA-90. [15]. Also: Beyer source by Tompkins; tape one is missing, so ID-156345 supplies patches and the encore [15]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-07-25 Compton Terrace Amphitheatre, Tempe, AZ, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-07-25-compton-terrace-amphitheatre-tempe-az-usa/) [29]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1982-07-25 Sun Compton Terrace, Tempe, AZ](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1396558529480/grateful-dead-1982-07-25-sun-compton) [30]
- Fan art by sandcastlesandglasscamels.blogspot.com: [7-25-82 Compton Terrace Amphitheatre, Tempe, AZ](https://sandcastlesandglasscamels.blogspot.com/2010/06/7-25-82-compton-terrace-amphitheatre.html) [31]

claims.text: Reviewer rates this Crazy Fingers below the Ventura or Red Rocks versions, though Tempe was always fun
An airport sits behind the stage at Tempe's Compton Terrace
Reviewer recalls the 1980 Compton Terrace second set as the best of the Tempe shows
Reviewer says the Compendium undersold this show, calling it a fine representation of a 1982 show
Sound is fine to good and easy to listen to
Forgetful singing in the opener suggests Jerry was in a happy mood that day
Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound great
Jerry fumbles three verses, but his and Brent's instrumental section is amazing
Reviewer singles out the Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance pairing as well worth hearing
Reviewer loves the Half-Step opener
The transition from Black Peter into Good Lovin' is called excellent
Audience recording quality is described as outstanding, putting you in the room
Reviewer ranks it among the top shows of 1982
Bobby sang a line about freedom not coming easy and a 25 cent cup of coffee, lifting a grieving listener
Maybe a small stumble in Crazy Fingers, since the band had just started playing it
Reviewer calls the sound good
Mr. Wise used Sennheiser 421 microphones, which reviewer prefers over Nakamichi shotguns
Heads who traveled from Tempe to Red Rocks two days later raved about this show
Taped with a Nakamichi 300, Schley source; patched using ID-80279 and ID-18481 for the encore
Minor tape damage in the left channel affects the first 2:37 of Candyman
From Jim Vita's master cassettes, transferred by Charlie Miller, with a Wise and Miller Sennheiser 421 patch in Estimated Prophet
Weir stays on stage with Billy and Mickey before Drums begins
Shure SM57 source from Ken Kelley's master cassettes, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Sennheiser 421 patches in Estimated Prophet, Drums and Space
Weir remains on stage with Billy and Mickey before Drums
Beyer source by Tompkins; tape one is missing, so ID-156345 supplies patches and the encore
